_comment: Board of Directors. Order in this list is the order shown on the About page. Leave 'photo' empty to show a placeholder.

members.name: Pamela Baird
members.bio: Pamela Baird has been a resident of Mountain View since 1998. She has enjoyed the challenges and rewards of being a business owner for over thirty-five years. Six years ago she reduced the scope of the business, which has allowed more time to do other things. Pamela has served on the Human Relations Commission and the Environmental Planning Commission. Travel, arts of all kinds, exercise, and volunteering are important parts of her daily life. Researching women's suffrage efforts in Mountain View has been a favourite project.

members.name: Robert Cox
members.bio: Robert was a project lead for Intel Compilers and Languages at Intel Corporation in Santa Clara, and retired in October 2024 to devote himself to community activities. He holds a PhD in Systems Engineering from Case Western Reserve University. Robert served on the Mountain View Planning Commission from 2013–2020 and, since 2023, as an appointed member of the Rental Housing Committee. He is Chair of the Old Mountain View Neighborhood Association, having served as Vice Chair from 2011 to 2024, and is a member of the Steering Committee of Livable Mountain View. Robert writes two genealogy columns for the MVHA newsletter and organises Neighborhood Social Outreach for the Association.

members.name: Anthea Chung
members.bio: Anthea joins the Mountain View Historical Association as Treasurer, bringing over 20 years of experience in finance and accounting as a CPA. She grew up in Hong Kong and has been proud to call Mountain View home since 2000, where she and her husband raised two children who both graduated from Mountain View High School. Anthea values giving back to the community she has been part of for so many years and is excited to help steward the Association's finances in support of its mission.

members.name: Jamil Shaikh
members.bio: Jamil has been a lifetime member of the Association since 2002. He holds a bachelor's degree in Electronics Engineering and has extensive experience working in many facets of the electronics industry. He says that knowing the history of a place gives one a sense of belonging to the community.

members.name: Nick Perry
members.bio: Nick has volunteered on the MVHA Board of Directors since 2011, serving as Newsletter Editor (2011–15), Vice President (2016–18), and President (2018–20). He currently serves as Past President and volunteers as the Association's graphic designer and social media manager. Nick has a passion for the history of the built environment and holds a Master of City Planning and a Bachelor's in Urban Studies from UC Berkeley. A native of Mountain View, he has written two books on his hometown's history. In 2020, after twelve years as an urban designer for the San Francisco Planning Department, Nick joined the Santa Clara Valley Open Space Authority.

members.name: Lisa Roquero Garcia
members.bio: Lisa grew up in Mountain View and is a graduate of Los Altos High School and the University of California, Berkeley. She spent most of her life in Mountain View, where she raised her two children, both graduates of Mountain View High School. Lisa was a founding member of Mesa de la Comunidad, a nonprofit group that provided translation services to Latino families during the debates over closing a school in the district in the early 2000s. She stays connected to the Mountain View community through her volunteer work for the MVHA.

members.name: David Salinero
members.bio: David is a native of Mountain View, where he attended Landels Elementary, Graham Junior High, and Mountain View High School at the Castro campus. His ancestors immigrated to the SF Bay Area in the early 1900s, and his family has lived in Mountain View since 1928. David's interest in history and photography was inspired by his relatives and teachers. After graduating from San Jose State University, he had a 45-year career as a software professional in Silicon Valley.

members.name: John Cortez
members.bio: John Cortez is a longtime Mountain View resident and alumnus of Mountain View High School. In addition to supporting the MVHA he is a member and past Jr. President of Redwood Parlor #66, Native Sons of the Golden West. He is a strong supporter of history and has attended the San Francisco History Expo on their behalf.

members.name: IdaRose Sylvester
members.bio: IdaRose has lived in Mountain View for over 20 years, and is fascinated by the rapid change the city has gone through and its commitment to community. She holds an MBA, previously ran her own consulting firm, and now runs her nonprofit, Appetite for Good. She chairs Mountain View's Human Relations Commission and is involved in several civic organisations helping protect and define the city's future. She loves studying the past to see what lessons we can bring to the future.

members.name: Carol Donahue
members.bio: As the child of immigrants, Carol learned the value of preserving family and community history by hearing about her parents' journeys from outsiders to English-speaking US citizens. Maya Angelou's statement 'If you don't know where you've come from, you don't know where you're going' inspires Carol to share family lore with kinsfolk. Carol moved from Chicago to Mountain View in 2014 to be near family. She has worked in communications, editing, event management and administration in corporate and nonprofit settings, and served as a Business Volunteer for the Arts through the Arts and Business Council. Carol is past chair and current member of Mountain View's Performing Arts Committee.

members.name: Melanie Kaye
members.bio: Melanie is a retired art director, graphic designer, and a longtime resident of Mountain View. She studied design at the University of Cincinnati and went on to a career in advertising, followed by several years as a design instructor at Mission College in Santa Clara. Retirement has allowed her the time to research and share local history. She is co-author of Palmita Park: The First 100 Years, chronicling the history of a 1920s housing development in Old Mountain View. She strongly believes there is value in building a better future on the foundation of smart historic preservation.

members.name: Your name here
members.bio: The MVHA welcomes interested individuals to join our Board of Directors. Current vacancies include special committees appointed directly by our President. In the past these have included Programs, Memorials & Remembrances, Hospitality and Donations. If you have interest or experience in any of these areas, contact us today — email info@mountainviewhistorical.org or leave a voicemail at (650) 903-6890.
